name: Halberdiers
headerMeta: Silver era · Pike/Polearm infantry · anti-cav · 165 leadership · Honor Tree
pitch: A cost-effective anti-cavalry pike unit that dominates fights when kept in tight phalanx formation and properly braced. Vulnerable to crowd control, shielded units, and flanks — requires a screening partner and careful micro to stay effective.

doctrines.name: Anti-Cavalry Doctrine V
doctrines.note: −35% DMG taken from cavalry while bracing, +DMG vs cavalry while bracing

doctrines.name: Anti-Cavalry Brace Doctrine
doctrines.note: −30% DMG taken from cavalry when using brace-type skills

doctrines.name: Bleeding Brace Doctrine
doctrines.note: bracing inflicts bleeding on cavalry: 16% max HP + 400 DMG

veterancy.label: Bottom line
veterancy.body: Improves bracing — the unit spends most combat time braced, making this the primary choice.

veterancy.label: Top line
veterancy.body: Improves the charge ability, which has low damage and limited tactical value.

battleRole.positioning: Pair Halberdiers with another unit that screens them from flanks — they cannot solo-hold a line. {2} In tight phalanx formation, each model can hit two enemies; overwhelmed by too many targets and they break. {2} Stay behind cover when possible.
battleRole.formation: Default F2 (phalanx/block): sustained damage and attack speed far exceed loose formation; formation issues can be largely avoided with correct positioning. {2} Requires all unit models to be at the X-move position to form properly. {2} F1 (loose) serves burst impact damage vs charging cavalry, but vulnerable to CC and weak if the initial burst doesn't kill. {2} If caught off-guard mid-formation, pressing V (defensive stance cancel) can be better than bracing in a bad position. {2}
battleRole.tips: Stun-on-brace doctrine is must-have. {2} Braced Halberdiers automatically face nearby enemies, reducing the need to worry about flanking. {2} Charge ability should only be used from F1 with immediate post-hit brace; attempting from phalanx causes the unit to re-form mid-fight and gets them killed. {2} Weak block-break makes shielded units a serious problem. {2}

cards.name: Imperial Spear Guard
cards.why: advance order directly counters brace-type skills, safe frontal knockdown

cards.name: shielded units
cards.why: weak block-break makes these units a problem

controls.notes: Core formation micro: move from F2 to F2 during the fight and let it brace — requires all models at X-move position to form properly. {1} If F2-to-F2 is too hard or the fight moves too fast, swap to F1 and insta-brace. {1} Braced units auto-turn to face nearby enemies, reducing the burden on manual facing. {2} Undocumented micro trick: while braced in phalanx, pressing C then Space shifts to loose formation while retaining phalanx's damage bonus — creator found this untested in live play, treat as experimental. {2}

gaps: No fight-type strength ratings (Blob/Flank/Skirmish/Duelling) present in any source.
